body:
“Alpha, your King claimed a mate bond last night." My men said.
“The Apex doesn’t have a mate,” I heard myself say. “His bloodline is too dominant. Everyone knows the tradition.” 
The Apex Gideon Crossbane. A King who bends nations and wolves alike
“Apparently, everyone was wrong.” His voice was gentle, almost pitying. “The bond manifested last night. At your Alpha ceremony.” 
Something in his tone made me go still. “With who?”
“With Isla Rosewood.” 
The room suddenly tilted.
Last night. After I had destroyed Isla. After I had stood in front of hundreds of wolves and claimed another woman while she watched. 
The Apex had found my Isla at her most vulnerable, and the mate bond had snapped into place. 
“Where is she now?” I demanded. 
“Her apartment, as far as we know. But Alpha, you should be aware… the Apex has made it very clear that Isla is under his protection. Any wolf who approaches her will be considered a threat.”
---
I heard his name before I saw the trouble coming.
"Crossbane is going to be there." The taller one, red dress, Sylvia crest at her collar. "The actual Apex. At the induction." 
"I heard." Her friend, dark lipstick, diamond earrings, the kind of bored confidence that came from never having been told no. "Can you imagine? Being claimed by someone like that?"

"Practically impossible. Wolves like him don't look twice at anyone below Beta bloodline."

I was reaching past them for a glass of water. 

That was all, just water, trying to get through the next hour without dying of the social exhaustion that came from being the only packless wolf in a room full of people who knew exactly where they stood, when the taller one clocked me hovering at the edge of their conversation.

"Sorry." Already stepping back. "I didn’t mean to interrupt."

"Were you listening in on our conversation?" Diamond earrings regarded me the way you regarded something you weren't sure was worth your attention. 

"Just reaching for the water."

"Right." A pause as she looked me up and down.

“You're Isla, aren't you? Jaxon's little translator?"

Of course. There it was.

"I work with him, yes."

"Must be nice." Red dress, tilting her head. "Getting to be in his orbit. Even if it is just, you know." A gesture. Professional. 

Something made me say it. Maybe exhaustion. Maybe years of standing at the edges of rooms like this one, swallowing things that deserved to be said out loud. 

"I was actually just thinking–" Keeping my voice light. "A wolf as powerful as Gideon Crossbane probably doesn't see much difference between us. We're all the same to someone at that level." 

Dead silence. 

Then diamond earrings laughed. Not warmly.

"Oh that's sweet." She exchanged a look with her friend. "She thinks she's the same as us." 

"I didn't say–“ 

"Honey." Red dress stepped closer. Not threatening. Worse, it was pitying. 

“There is a very big difference between us and you. We have a Pack. We have bloodline. We have wolves who will claim us." Her eyes traveled down me again with the leisurely cruelty of someone who had never needed to hurry. 

"What do you have? You're Packless. Mateless. You don't even exist in our world except as the person Jaxon Ashford calls when he needs his paperwork translated." 

"Wolves like the Apex?" Diamond earrings smiled. "They don't see you at all. You're not invisible to them– no, wait, you're beneath invisible. They step on wolves like you without  even noticing."

My face was hot. My hands were completely still at my sides.

"At least we have access to higher wolves," red dress continued, like she was making a reasonable point in a reasonable conversation. 

"Chosen mates, futures, positions worth having." She tilted her glass slightly, just slightly. 

"You have nothing. You are nothing. And everyone in this room knows it."

The wine hit me before I registered the motion.

White. Cold. Down my front in one smooth pour that absolutely could have been accidental if you weren't watching her hand, and everyone nearby was very carefully not watching her hand.

"Oh no." Perfectly blank eyes. The exact same expression women had been using to destroy each other for centuries. "I'm so clumsy. I'm so sorry."

The murmur that moved through the nearby crowd was not sympathy.

I stood there with wine dripping from my dress and my eyes found Jaxon across the room.

He had seen. I knew him well enough to know that.

But what he did broke my heart into a million pieces.

He turned back to his conversation.

I rushed to the bathroom because it felt like the only place to escape to. 

The marble was cold under my hands.

I gripped the sink and looked at myself in the mirror and the woman looking back at me had wine on her dress and mascara that hadn't smudged yet but was going to, and I thought about what red dress had said.

You are nothing.

He doesn't see you at all.

I pressed my eyes shut.

He cares. He just can't show it right now. The timing isn't right. He's in a delicate position and I understand that, I've always understood that, and when the induction is done everything will be different–

He cares.

He swears he cares.

I turned the tap on and pressed a cold cloth against the stain and told myself that this was the price of something worth having. 

That the women in that room didn't know what we had. 

That the way he saw me when no one was watching was real, that the promises he made were real, that the boy who kissed me in the ashes and said you and me, always was still somewhere inside the polished Alpha playing the long game.

He loves me.

He swears he loves me.

Everything will be okay.

That's what I always believed. 

Until the night it all came crumbling down.

II Chapter 2: The First Love’s Betrayal
ISLA

I told myself tonight was different.

I've been telling myself that a lot lately.

After the Sylvia incident, after the wine and the blank eyes and you are nothing delivered with a smile, I had spent three days convincing myself that what happened was an aberration. 

That the women were cruel and the room was wrong and Jaxon had been caught off guard, hadn't known what to do, couldn't cause a scene without risking everything he'd worked toward.

He'd called the next morning. Said he was sorry. Said he'd seen it and hated it and hated himself for not stepping in.

I believed him.

That was the thing about Jaxon Ashford; I always believed him.

So I wore the dress he sent. 

Champagne silk, expensive, the note tucked inside reading tonight changes everything.

I stood at the back of the most beautiful ballroom I'd ever been in with my heart in my throat and eight years of waiting concentrated into one evening and I told myself… 

This is it. This is the night.

The ceremony was everything Jaxon had described. 

Kieran Blackwell – silver-haired, The Judge – taking the stage, the crowd hushing like a current had passed through it. Alphas and Lunas in designer everything leaning forward as Jaxon walked in.

He was magnificent.

Sharp suit. Silver insignia. Every wolf in the room deferring without being asked.

Look at me, I thought. Just once. You don't have to say my name. Just let me know you see me standing here.

His gaze swept the room.

Passed right over me.

Protocol, I told myself. Just protocol.

He delivered his speech – perfectly rehearsed, every pause landing exactly where it should – and I stood at the back and let myself feel it, the pride of knowing him. Of having been beside him for all the years that built toward this moment, even if no one in this room knew that. 

Even if I was invisible here too.

It didn't matter.

After tonight, everything would be different.

Then his tone shifted.

"Which is why–" A pause, deliberate, the whole room breathing with him. "It is also my great honor to announce my engagement."

The floor dropped out from under me. 

"To Evelyn Harrington, daughter of Alpha Henry Harrington."

The applause was deafening.

I didn't hear it.

A woman stepped to his side. Polished, radiant, a diamond catching every light in the room. 

Jaxon's hand settled on her waist – possessive, proud, practiced – and he smiled at her the way he used to smile at me when no one was watching.

You are nothing.

The words from three nights ago landed differently now. Because those women had known, hadn't they? 

Everyone in that room had probably known. I was the only one who hadn't. 

I found myself already moving.  

I don't remember crossing the ballroom. I just ended up there, at the edge of the stage, looking up at him. 

He looked down.

Our eyes met.

I searched his face for the boy who kissed me in the ashes and said you and me, always.

He wasn't there.

"Jaxon." My voice came out too small for this room. "You promised me." 

Something flickered. Gone before I could name it.

"Not here, Isla." Quiet. Clipped.

"Eight years–“

"This is how it has to be."

People were staring. I could feel it pressing on my skin and I didn't care, I didn't care about any of it, I only cared that he was standing there with another woman's hand in his and looking at me like I was a problem to be managed. 

"Look me in the eye. Tell me you don't love me."

Silence. 

"I'm sorry." Soft. Final. The voice of someone who had already moved on. 

"But I need you to leave."

Someone called his name from across the stage. 

He turned – he actually turned away from me – and let the room pull him back in. 

Evelyn moved with him. Her smile never wavered.

He didn't look back.

I turned and ran. 

— 

The terrace was cold and I was grateful for it.

I crashed through the door and grabbed the railing and pressed my face into the night air and tried to remember how to breathe. 

Eight years. Eight years and a note that said 

tonight changes everything and champagne silk and the absolute, devastating realization that I had been the only one counting.

The sob that came out of me was ugly, but I didn't care.

"Pathetic," I heard myself say. "You are so pathetic, Isla."

"I disagree." 

I spun around. 

A man stood in the shadows at the far end of the terrace. Tall. Broad-shouldered. Eyes so pale they were almost silver in the dark, catching what little light there was and holding it.

I knew who he was before I could think.

Everyone knew who he was.

Gideon Crossbane.

The Apex.

The wolf those women had invoked three nights ago like a name you said to remind someone of their smallness.

Wolves like the Apex step on you like you’re nothing. 

"I– I didn't know anyone was out here," I managed. 

"I know." Low. Controlled. "You… should go back inside."

Something in me – raw and wrecked and completely finished with being told where to be – refused.

"Why?" I choked out. "So I can watch him celebrate?"

He went very still. 

The air between us changed. Something I didn’t have a word for, something that moved through my chest like a frequency I'd been hearing at the edge of my whole life and had only now turned toward.

“Isla, you need to go back inside."

Quieter this time.

Like the instruction was for himself as much as for me, like any second more that I stayed here would cost him something…

Cost me something. 

III Chapter 3: The Unexpected Mate
ISLA

He steps forward.

Slow. Deliberate. Crosses the terrace toward me like someone who has made a decision they cannot take back. Stops close enough that I can see the scar through his left eyebrow, the tight set of his jaw, the way every muscle in him is working to hold something in check. 

"Look at me." Low. Almost gentle.

I don't know why I do it.

His eyes find mine.

And the world cracks open.

Nothing like what I felt for Jaxon. That was warmth, familiarity, eight years of someone becoming part of my landscape until I couldn't picture the view without them. 

This is something else entirely; a thread pulled taut from somewhere deep in my chest, a pull so fierce it steals the breath from my lungs before I can think to hold onto it.

Mine, something in me says. 

It terrifies me how much I mean it.

His breath changes. Barely perceptible. He felt it too.

His hand moves, lifting toward my face, and stops.

He steps back.

Something flickers through his expression. Not rejection. The thing that lives underneath rejection; closer to pain, to restraint, to a man fighting himself and winning by the narrowest possible margin.

"Run." His voice drops to something raw. "Isla. Now. Before I do something we both regret."

"What are you–“ 

“Please.” 

That one word – wrecked, quiet, like it cost him everything he had – gets me moving.

I run.

— 

I don't remember the drive home.

One moment I was pushing through gilded hallways with my heart in pieces, the next I was standing in my apartment with my keys still in my hand and no memory of the space between. 

The apartment looked exactly as I'd left it. Small. Ordinary. Books on the coffee table, half-empty mug from this morning, the life of a woman who'd been holding her breath for eight years waiting for it to start.

I stood in the center of it.

Then I walked to the kitchen and turned on the gas stove.

The champagne silk caught fast; blackening at the edges, the embroidery curling into nothing, the careful stitching someone had spent hours on dissolving in seconds. 

I dropped it in the sink and watched it go. The smoke alarm shrieked. I waved it quiet and stood there watching the ashes spiral down the drain. 

Wear this. Tonight changes everything.

He'd been right about that.

My phone rang. Lena. I watched it ring out, her name pulsing on the screen like a question I didn't have an answer to yet.

She called again. I watched that one go too.

I changed out of the ruined remains of the evening; sweatpants, an oversized shirt, the version of myself that existed before induction balls and eight years of waiting, and sank onto the couch. Drew my knees up. Let the apartment go quiet around me.

Jaxon's hand on Evelyn's waist. Possessive. Proud.

You are nothing, the women at the Sylvia estate had said, three nights and a lifetime ago. 

I hadn't believed them then. 

I pressed the heels of my hands against my eyes until I saw shapes instead of images.

My phone lit up. A text from Lena, my best friend: Isla, what’s going on? What happened with Jaxon? Are you okay?

I typed back: I’ll tell you when I can, Lena. I can’t right now. 

Three dots. Then: Okay. I’m here for you, you know that right? You’re going to be okay.

I hope so, I sent back. Just not tonight.

A longer pause. Then: Call me when you're ready. I don't care what time.

I set the phone face-down on the cushion beside me.

Outside, the city was doing what it always did; moving, indifferent, unbothered by whatever catastrophe was happening inside any given window. 

Somewhere across town, a ballroom full of wolves was still celebrating. Jaxon was probably still smiling. Evelyn's diamond was still catching the light.

And I was here. Sweatpants. Ash under my fingernails.

I tipped my head back against the couch and stared at the ceiling.

The silver-eyed man on the terrace.

Run. Before I do something we both regret.

I did run, but a part of me keeps thinking if I hadn’t. 

And the pull –  that terrifying, impossible thread – hadn't diminished even slightly with the distance between us. 

If anything it felt sharper now. More present. Like something that knew exactly where I was and was noting the information carefully. 

I told myself it didn't matter. 

I told myself a lot of things that night.

I sat in the quiet apartment until my eyes stopped burning and the worst of the evening settled into something I could almost breathe around.

Tomorrow, I'd figure out what to do with all of it.

Tonight I just needed everything to stop moving.

I almost managed it.

And then, somewhere between one breath and the next, I thought about the way he'd said please, like the word had been wrung out of him against his will, and I understood, in the way you understood things you weren't ready to understand yet, that the man on the terrace was not done with me.

And neither, if I was honest with myself, was whatever I'd felt when his eyes found mine. 

I wasn't ready to be honest with myself about that.

Not tonight.

IV Chapter 4: Meeting The Impossible
GIDEON

I smelled her before I saw her.

Jasmine and salt and something else underneath; grief, raw and unmanaged, the scent of someone who'd stopped trying to hold it together. 

I stepped onto the terrace for air, as I sometimes did at these events when the density of ambition in a room became its own kind of suffocation. The terrace was supposed to be empty.

She was there instead. 

Collapsed against the railing with her shoulders shaking, her champagne silk dress wrinkled, her hair coming loose from whatever arrangement it had started the night in. 

I should have retreated immediately. Given her the space. Come back in ten minutes when the moment had passed.

I didn't move.

Because the moment she turned and her eyes found mine, every carefully constructed wall I'd spent thirty years building developed a crack straight down the center.

My wolf surged forward with a violence I hadn't felt in years.

MINE.

I forced it back through sheer discipline. Gripped the railing. Kept my face neutral while my internal world rearranged itself around a woman I had never spoken to in my life.

I knew who she was. Dorian always knew everything worth knowing, and he briefed me months ago when Ashford's various arrangements became relevant to the induction proceedings. 

Isla. Beta's daughter. Packless; never formally claimed by any Alpha. Ashford's secret for the better part of a decade, kept close and kept hidden, and just publicly discarded in front of the entire Pack world without so much as a flinch.

My mate, something in me said. He had his hands on my mate for eight years.

I had watched the ballroom scene from across the room. Had watched her walk to the edge of that stage and asked him for something as she looked him in the eye. Had watched him turn away.

The rage that came with that memory now was not something I was prepared for. 

I told her to go back inside.

She didn't.

Of course she didn't.

She already had, by my understanding, a brutal week.

Dorian's intelligence had mentioned something about an incident at the Sylvia estate three nights prior, women and a ruined dress and Ashford doing nothing while it happened.

And now this. 

Publicly, completely, discarded.

She had nothing left to lose tonight, and she wasn't interested in one more person telling her where to be.

She stood there with the expression of someone expecting one more disappointment. 

And I found myself stepping forward anyway.

I couldn't help it. That was the honest truth of it; Gideon Crossbane, the Apex of the Untouchable Seven, a man who had spent three decades being told that control was the only currency that mattered, and I could not stop myself from crossing a terrace toward a crying woman in a ruined dress.

“Look at me.”

She did exactly that. 

And the bond roared to life between us so completely it nearly knocked me off my feet. 

I watched her pupils blow wide. Watched the confusion hit first, then the recognition, that thread pulling taut, that frequency neither of us had chosen. 

She felt it. All of it.

I could see the exact moment it landed, the way her hand pressed against her sternum like she was trying to hold something in.

My hand moved toward her face before I had even made the decision to move it.

I managed to stop it and stepped back.

Because she was broken right now. Because she had spent eight years on a man who'd chosen power over her, twice now that I understood, and done it publicly both times without looking back. 

Because claiming her at this moment, using what she was feeling against her, would make me exactly the kind of man she just ran from. 

She deserved a choice.

"Run," I managed. "Isla. Before I do something we both regret."

She hesitated.

"Please.”

And then she ran.

I stood on the terrace and watched her disappear through the door and felt the bond stretch and scream in protest. 

Below, the city continued being indifferent. From inside, I could hear Ashford's name being toasted with expensive champagne, by people who would be toasting a different name within five years if I had anything to do with it. 

I pressed my hands flat on the railing.

She was somewhere in this city. Alone. 

The bond pulled like a compass needle finding north, insisting on direction, insisting I had somewhere to be and that somewhere was not a terrace.

I should give her the night. That was the reasonable thing.

I pushed off the railing. 

I was going to find her anyway.

— 

The address Dorian sent me belonged to the kind of building that said I live within my means and I've stopped apologizing for it.

Clean. Quiet. The sort of street where people minded their own business by mutual agreement.

I stood outside her door longer than I'd admit to anyone.

In the space of twenty minutes on a terrace, I had lost thirty years of composure entirely.

The bond pulled. Insistent. 

I knocked.

Silence. Then movement; the quality of someone who heard the knock and was deciding what to do with it.

"Jaxon, I don't want to–"

"It's not Jaxon."

A longer silence.

"How do you know where I live?"

"Does it matter right now?"

The longest pause yet. I waited. 

In all my years as the Apex, I was never considered the waiting type, but apparently, for a woman I had only known for a few hours, I was willing to do it. 

To wait for as long as I needed. 

And then, like a prayer answered… 

The door opened. 

V Chapter 5: After Everything
ISLA

Sweatpants. Hair down. Mascara faintly tracked at the corner of my eyes. The expression of someone who had used up her capacity for surprise.

That was me, looking back at him. 

Gideon Crossbane stood in my doorway still in his suit from the ceremony, tie gone, collar open, silver eyes finding mine, and I felt it again immediately; that pull, that infuriating thread that had no business existing between me and a man I had met an hour ago on a terrace.

I stepped back. Let him in.

Because I already burned the dress and cried in front of a stranger and apparently my decision-making tonight was operating without its usual safeguards.

He took in the apartment in one sweep; the books, the small space, the ordinary life of someone still in the waiting room of her real one, and didn't comment on any of it. 

Just stood in the center of my living room, waiting.

I crossed my arms.

"You burnt something." His eyes went to the kitchen.

"The dress. His dress." I shrugged with a steadiness I didn't fully feel. "I didn't want it anymore."

"Good."  

I blinked. "Good?"

"It was his. You don't keep things from people who use them as currency." 

I stared at him. That was… accurate. More accurate than anything I'd managed to think all night.

"Why are you here?" I asked, a slight bitter tone in my voice.

"You know why." 

"I want you to say it."

"You're my mate." Simple. The way you stated facts about weather or distance. "I felt the bond on the terrace. You felt it too. I'm not going to stand here and pretend otherwise."

"I don't want a mate." The words came out harder than I meant them, and I watched something shift in his expression; not hurt, something more careful than that.

“I don't want any of this. I wanted–" I stopped.

"Him," Gideon said quietly.

"Yes." It cost something to say it out loud.

"I wanted him. For eight years. And this week alone I've had wine poured on me by women who called me nothing, and I've watched him look at his phone while it happened, and tonight he–" My voice threatened to break. I managed to not let it.

“So forgive me if I'm not in the mood to hear about the universe's alternative arrangements." 

Something moved through his face. Not pity. Something sharper.

"Someone poured a drink on you." Not a question.

"It's not important." 

"It's important to me."

My eyes found him properly for the first time since he'd walked in. 

Really found him, the way his jaw had tightened, the barely contained fury sitting just under the surface of his composure.

"Why would that matter to you?" I asked. "You don't know me."

"I know enough." His voice was low. "I know you stood at the edge of a stage tonight and looked a man who betrayed you in the eye. I know that took more courage than most wolves in that room will ever have to find in their lives."

I didn't have anything to say to that.

He took one step toward me. Just one. 

And the pull intensified, that magnetic current, and I felt my body lean toward him before my mind caught up. I took a deliberate step back.

His jaw tightened. He felt that too.

"Don't."

"I'm not doing anything."

"You're standing there. Being whatever you are. And it's making it very hard to think." 

Something moved in his expression; not quite a smile, the thing that lived in the same place a smile would, if the moment allowed for it.

"I affect you." Not arrogant. Like he was filing away information he hadn't expected.

"Don't make it a thing."

"I'm not making it anything. I'm noting that it goes both ways."

"I guess that’s the bond."

"Is it only the bond?"

I opened my mouth. Closed it.

He held my gaze steadily. Silver eyes in the low light of my ordinary apartment, the most powerful wolf alive standing in front of my secondhand bookshelves, and I had absolutely no framework for tonight.

"I don't know what to do with you," I admitted.

"You don't have to know tonight." He loosened his collar slightly, the only sign he was anything less than completely composed. "I just didn't want you to be alone with all of it."

"With what?"

"With what they did to you. What he did to you." Direct. Unflinching. "It should be witnessed. Even by a stranger."

"You're not a stranger. You're the Apex."

"I can be both."

Something about the simplicity of that landed somewhere unexpected.

"I need it to be slow. Whatever this is. I need it to go very, very slowly."

A long pause.

"Okay."

Just that. No negotiation, no conditions.

"Okay?" I repeated. 

"Slow." A confirmation. "I can do slow."

He said it like it cost him something. Like slow was the hardest instruction he'd ever been given.

I believed him. 

I moved to the couch. Sat. After a moment, I glanced at the other end of it.

He followed and sat.

The pull between us settled into something almost bearable at this distance; still there, still pulling, but no longer threatening to knock me sideways. 

Outside, the city moved through its midnight business. 

In here, something that couldn't be taken back had already quietly begun.

I wasn’t sure if I liked the thought of that or not. 

VI Chapter 6: Impossible To Resist
ISLA 

He didn't move from the couch.

I'd expected him to push; some version of Jaxon's careful, practiced patience that always somehow got him what he wanted eventually.

Gideon just sat there with his hands loosely clasped between his knees, watching me with an attention that felt different from anything I had experienced. Not performing patience.

Actually being patient.

"I loved him." The words scraped on the way out. "For eight years, I loved him."

"I know."

"He promised me forever."

"He lied."

Something in me wanted to argue that, defend it, defend eight years of my life from being reduced to two words. But he wasn't wrong.

"And you?" My chin came up. Whatever defiance I had left was going to show up now or not at all. 

"What are you promising me? What pretty words do Alphas like you use to get what you want?"

"None." He held my gaze steadily. "I'm not going to make you promises I might not keep. I'm not going to tell you this will be easy, or that caring about me won't come with complications. I'm the Apex. My life is politics and power plays and enemies who'd use you to get to me." 

"Then why should I choose you over him?"

"Because I'll never hide you." Simple. Direct. "Because I'll never make you feel like you're not enough. Because when I claim you, the entire world will know you're mine. No secrets. No shame. No waiting in the shadows while I pretend you don't exist."

I was silent for a long moment. Weighing it. Trying to reconcile what my wolf was telling me with what the rest of me still wanted, even now, even after everything.

"I don't love you." Finally. 

"I know."

"I might never love you."

Something flickered across his face; there and gone. "I know that too."

"So why are you still here?"

"Because the bond gives us time." His voice stayed even. "Time for you to heal from what he did. Time to get to know me. Time to decide if this, us, is something you want to choose. I'm not asking you to love me tonight. I'm asking you not to shut the door completely."

I studied him. Tried to see past the composure to whatever was underneath it.

"What do you want from me?" I asked quietly. "Right now. Tonight. What do you actually want?"

Something moved behind his eyes; quick, contained, gone before I could name it.

"I want you to let me stay. Just for tonight. On your couch, fully clothed. I want to know you're safe and not alone with all of this."

"That's it?" 

"That's it."

"You just want to sit on my couch?"

"If you'll let me."

I regarded him like he might be insane. The Apex, asking permission to sleep on a couch that folded out into something distinctly unglamorous.

"You could compel me." Slowly. "You're an Alpha. You could use your influence and I'd have to agree."

"I could." No hesitation. "But I won't. Your choice, Isla. Always your choice."

Another silence. Longer this time.

"Okay," I heard myself say. "You can stay."

Something crossed his face; relief, unguarded for just a second before he reined it back in. 

"Thank you."

"But you stay on the couch," I added quickly. "And you leave first thing in the morning. And this doesn't mean I'm accepting the bond or agreeing to anything or–“ 

"Understood." The corner of his mouth moved. Not quite a smile. "Just tonight."

I found a pillow and blanket and threw them at him like they might bite. "It folds out but it's not very comfortable."

"It's fine."

"And the bathroom's down the hall if you–“ 

"I can figure it out. Thank you.” 

We stood there a moment, the space between us doing the thing it kept doing. The Apex, in my living room, holding a pillow that smelled like fabric softener, looking as unsure of the next move as I felt.

"I'm going to bed."

"Goodnight, Isla." 

I started toward my bedroom. Stopped at the doorway.

"Gideon?"

"Yes?"

"Why did you tell me to run? On the terrace. Why not just–" I made myself finish it. "Claim me then?"

He met my eyes without flinching.

"Because you just had your heart broken. Because you were vulnerable and hurting, and taking advantage of that would make me no better than him. Because even though every instinct I had was screaming at me to mark you right there, I knew you deserved better than being claimed by a stranger in the worst moment of your life."

Something in my chest loosened. Just slightly.

"Oh."

"Sleep well, Isla."

I didn't answer this time. I slipped into my bedroom and closed the door softly behind me, and stood there for a moment with my back against it, listening to him move around in the living room; the couch unfolding, fabric settling, a man twice my size trying to make himself smaller in an unfamiliar space.

The bond hummed. Quiet now. Steady.

I climbed into bed and lay there in the dark, and somewhere on the other side of my door, the most powerful wolf in the pack world was arranging himself on a couch that was definitely too short for him, because I'd asked him to and he'd simply said understood.

I didn't know what to do with that.

I closed my eyes.

But the bond had other plans.

It started as warmth; low in my chest, spreading outward the way heat spread from a fire you'd stopped noticing until you moved too close to it. 

I told myself it was exhaustion. Adrenaline finally leaving my body. Anything except what it actually was.

It got worse.

Fifteen feet away, through a wall and a closed door, I could feel him. 

The pull of him, insistent and low and unbearably warm, like something in me had reoriented itself entirely around the fact that he existed and was close and was, infuriatingly, exactly where I'd told him to be. 

I sat up.

This is insane, I told myself. You met him four hours ago.

But the bond didn't care about the timeline.

I found myself sitting on the edge of my bed with my feet already on the floor before I even registered standing up. My hand was on the doorframe before I'd decided to cross the room. 

Every rational thought I owned was screaming at me to lie back down, and every other part of me, the part that had felt the world crack open on a terrace, the part that had leaned toward him in my own living room before catching myself, was already reaching for the handle.

Just to see if he's still there, I told myself. Just to check.

That was a lie and I knew it was a lie even as I thought it.

I stood in the dark with my palm flat against my own door, breathing hard, feeling the pull on the other side of it like a current I could have followed with my eyes closed. 

He was right there. Fifteen feet. Maybe less.

I could go to him right now and neither of us would have to pretend anymore that whatever this was could be managed with a folded-out couch and good intentions.

My fingers curled around the handle.

body:
A dream is like a field of wild buckwheat, bathed in moonlight and kissed by frost. You are the one making your way toward it, traversing earthen slopes and following the delicate, ridged veins along the edges of the leaves. As long as the buckwheat remains, your path is the right one.

The journey of pursuing a dream is much like walking toward that field of wild buckwheat on a late-autumn, moonlit night. There may be moments of hesitation—when fallen leaves blanket the slope, obscuring the way forward—or quiet intervals when the night mist rises, causing the buckwheat to blend into the surrounding grasses, making it hard to discern. Yet, when the breeze stirs again, you can trace the fine, distinct ridges along the leaf margins to confirm that you are still on the right track. It is this interplay between tactile sensation and the deepening night that transforms you: from someone merely eager to reach the field, you become a nocturnal traveler who trusts that the wild buckwheat—marked by the ridges along its leaves—is waiting for you under the moonlight. 💪🌙 Whenever the wind falls still and the outlines of the buckwheat blur into the night mist, pause and gently brush your fingers along the edge of a leaf. You will feel a series of fine, sharp ridges—distinct and more defined than the surrounding wild vegetation—resembling a row of microscopic saw teeth, offering a subtle, tingling sensation. Follow the texture of these ridges through the darkness, and you will surely find the field.

One day, after crossing the final slope, the field of wild buckwheat will appear before you. Moonlight rests upon the tiny white blossoms, while the ridges along the leaf edges cast delicate, intricate shadows. You crouch down and pluck a single leaf, tracing its ridged margin with your fingertips. As you feel those fine, sharp contours beneath your skin, you look back across the slopes you traversed through the night—guided all the while by those very ridges—and you embrace, with a profound sense of peace, the version of yourself who, even when the buckwheat vanished time and again into the night, never lost the way, guided always by the ridges on the leaves. 🍂🌙 The most moving moment is not when moonlight falls upon a leaf, but rather the faith you hold—even when the buckwheat remains hidden from sight—that the fine, ridged veins brushing against your fingertips are leading you toward a field of wild buckwheat. Every leaf swallowed by the night will reappear beneath your touch the moment you arrive.

🌙 No matter how deep the darkness, it cannot obscure a field of wild buckwheat, marked by the delicate ridges along its leaf margins. No matter how long the earthen slope, it is no match for someone willing to reach out in the dark, tracing those edges and feeling the fine, intricate lines. Even if the buckwheat’s silhouette has vanished entirely into the night, keep walking along the slope. The ridges on the leaves will guide you; and as you reach the edge of the field, the moonlight will illuminate the very leaf you hold—revealing the delicate, angular veins beneath your fingers.

Do not stop simply because you cannot see; keep reaching, keep searching, until you arrive at your own moonlit field of wild buckwheat. 💥🌍 Even the longest slope can be traversed, one step at a time. Press onward—the ridged edges of the leaves are waiting for you just ahead. 🙌👇

🦷 Can fixed metal brackets complicate a digital restorative workflow?

In this clinical case, a 16-year-old orthodontic patient required a long-term provisional crown on an endodontically retreated lower right first molar.
The restorative treatment needed to be completed before mandibular orthodontic treatment could continue. At the same time, the clinical team had to capture the opposing arch through fixed metal brackets and an archwire.
Using the Clariscan UP610, the team captured digital impressions of both arches and transferred the scan data from the Soreal platform into exocad for provisional crown design.

The case follows the complete chairside workflow:
🔹 Digital impression around fixed orthodontic appliances
🔹 Detailed capture of the prepared tooth and margin
🔹 Open-format transfer into exocad
🔹 Resin nanoceramic provisional crown fabrication
🔹 Adhesive cementation and final clinical outcome

See how digital scanning supported restorative treatment while the patient's occlusion was still changing.

🔗 Read the full clinical case: https://www.up3dtech.com/en/events/case-study-restoring-an-endodontically-retreated-molar-with-a-longterm-provisional-crown-using-the-up610

body:
🔺 Là Brand, Trade, Sales Managers? 
Bạn quyết định ngân sách mỗi ngày từ khuyến mãi, truyền thông đến hỗ trợ bán hàng. Nhưng thiếu tư duy tài chính, mọi thứ dễ trở thành “cảm tính có hệ thống”: 
- Không rõ Net Sales Value là gì, không tính được lợi nhuận gộp. 
- Không phản biện được khi bị cắt ngân sách, cũng không thể thuyết phục sếp cũng như phòng tài chính duyệt đề án mới. 
- Tung sản phẩm thì kỳ vọng cao, nhưng không có công cụ để dự báo, tính ROI hay đánh giá hiệu quả sau cùng. 
Bạn không sai vì bạn không học tài chính. Nhưng nếu vẫn quản lý ngân sách mà không hiểu “ngôn ngữ tài chính”, bạn sẽ mãi ở thế bị động lãng phí nguồn lực mà không biết. 

📚 Khóa học "Finance for Non-Finance Managers" được CASK thiết kế sẽ giúp bạn giải quyết những điều gì?  
👉 TÌM HIỂU NGAY TẠI:  https://cask.vn/khoa-hoc/finance-for-non-finance/

1️⃣ Hiểu tổng thể chuỗi giá trị & 3 báo cáo tài chính nền tảng 
Không chỉ đơn thuần là học cách đọc báo cáo, mà còn hiểu mối liên hệ giữa các con số và hoạt động kinh doanh thực tế. Tư duy Value Chain giúp bạn xác định đâu là các mắt xích đang “ngốn” ngân sách, đâu là điểm tạo giá trị thật và làm quen với bộ 3 báo cáo tài chính quan trọng: 
- Balance Sheet (Bảng cân đối kế toán): Giúp bạn đánh giá cấu trúc vốn và tài sản để đưa ra quyết định đầu tư đúng đắn. 
- Profit & Loss (P&L - Báo cáo kết quả hoạt động kinh doanh): Giúp bạn nhìn rõ dòng chảy doanh thu – chi phí – lợi nhuận. 
- Cash Flow: Giúp bạn phân biệt được lợi nhuận kế toán với tiền mặt thật sự, tránh rủi ro “lãi ảo – cháy tiền thật”.
 
2️⃣ Ứng dụng P&L để tối ưu danh mục, lợi nhuận và giá trị ròng 
Hiểu sâu và phân tích được các yếu tố chính trong P&L, từ đó: 
- Điều chỉnh chính sách giá, chiến lược chiết khấu, ngân sách marketing. 
- Xác định sản phẩm nào cần giữ – phát triển – hay mạnh dạn cắt bỏ. 
Hiểu một vài chỉ số quan trọng như: 
- Net Sales Value (NSV) – doanh thu thực sự sau các khoản khuyến mãi. 
- Gross Margin (GM) – lợi nhuận gộp theo sản phẩm, danh mục hay ngành hàng. 
Từ đó biết cách áp dụng P&L như một bản đồ chiến lược tài chính để định hướng toàn bộ hoạt động marketing – bán hàng hiệu quả hơn.  

3️⃣ Lập kế hoạch tài chính theo chiến lược (Annual Operating Plan – AOP) 
Không còn là những bảng ngân sách “theo cảm tính”, bạn sẽ học cách xây dựng kế hoạch tài chính bài bản với: 
- Quy trình 7 bước xây dựng AOP – bảo đảm tính logic và liên kết giữa mục tiêu chiến lược và hành động cụ thể. 
- Hiểu rõ các phương pháp xây dựng ngân sách, biết cách phân bổ chi phí cho marketing, sales, nhân sự… phù hợp với chỉ tiêu kinh doanh. 
- Thực hành lập kế hoạch AOP qua bài tập mô phỏng thực tế, giúp bạn tự tin khi trình bày kế hoạch trước đội ngũ tài chính hoặc lãnh đạo cấp cao. 

4️⃣ Đo lường hiệu quả các hoạt động khuyến mãi, tung sản phẩm mới 
Cách đo lường hiệu quả tài chính một cách chính xác, không còn “dựa vào cảm giác” hay “phỏng đoán”. 
- Tính ROI (Return on Investment) cho các hoạt động truyền thông – khuyến mãi – activation. 
- Dự báo doanh thu khi launching sản phẩm mới với công cụ Sales Estimator. 
- Đánh giá hiệu quả (Post Launch Evaluation): Liệu sản phẩm mới có thật sự đáng để đầu tư tiếp? 
Khóa học dành cho ai? 
🔹 Brand, Trade, Sales Manager muốn đọc – những người thường xuyên đưa ra quyết định ảnh hưởng đến chi phí và lợi nhuận, nhưng chưa được đào tạo bài bản về tài chính.  
🔹 Chủ doanh nghiệp muốn nắm vững ngôn ngữ tài chính để kiểm soát dòng tiền, hiểu báo cáo và trao đổi hiệu quả với kế toán, CFO hoặc nhà đầu tư.  
🔹 Người đang muốn lên quản lý, nhưng thiếu nền tảng tài chính để bước vào các cuộc họp mang tính chiến lược. 
Đừng để tài chính là điểm yếu khiến bạn vụt mất cơ hội thăng tiến. Hãy làm chủ nó trước khi nó kiểm soát bạn. 

-----------------------

👉 Đăng ký nhận Tài liệu Chuyên sâu về Quản trị Tài chính cho CEO: https://hubs.ly/Q04zZF7f0 

Cắt giảm ngân sách cào bằng luôn là mệnh lệnh nhanh nhất để tối ưu báo cáo KQKD ngắn hạn. Nhưng trong dài hạn, đây lại là con đường ngắn nhất triệt hạ năng lực cạnh tranh cốt lõi.

Trước thềm chu kỳ biến động 2026 - 2027, bài toán của Nhà điều hành không nằm ở việc siết bao nhiêu tiền, mà là các quyết định mang tính sinh tồn: 
❓ Tại sao cắt giảm chi phí liên tục nhưng biên lợi nhuận vẫn bào mòn? 
❓ Đâu là "chi phí rác" cần triệt phá, đâu là "vốn chiến lược" bắt buộc phải bảo vệ để giữ đà tăng trưởng? 
❓ Làm sao né bẫy 79% doanh nghiệp cắt giảm thụ động thì gần 50% chi phí "bật nảy" trở lại sau 12 - 24 tháng (theo McKinsey)?

"Siết chi phòng thủ" đã lỗi thời. CEO hiện đại cần tái định hình tư duy: Chuyển từ cắt giảm cơ học sang Tái cấu trúc kiến trúc chi phí (Cost Architecture) và Tối ưu hóa Phân bổ Vốn (Capital Allocation).

🎯 Strategic Playbook: AGILE MARGIN 2027 được thiết kế chuẩn hóa cho cấp HĐQT & CEO qua 4 trụ cột điều hành:
🔸 Tái định hình Kiến trúc Chi phí từ Gốc: Ứng dụng tư duy Ngân sách gốc 0 (ZBB/ZBR) để tái cấu trúc dòng vốn vào đúng động cơ tăng trưởng thực. 
🔸 Bảo vệ Biên lợi nhuận Linh hoạt (Agile Margin): Thiết lập cơ chế ngưỡng kích hoạt tài chính (Trigger Metrics) giúp doanh nghiệp chủ động tái phân bổ ngân sách theo biến động thị trường. 
🔸 Quản trị Thực chiến từ Tập đoàn Toàn cầu: Giải mã các case study thành công trong bài toán tái cấu trúc vốn của các thương hiệu hàng đầu. 
🔸 Bộ chỉ số Kiểm toán Quản trị (Executive Audit): 10 câu hỏi chiến lược giúp CEO rà soát toàn diện sức khỏe tài chính và mô hình vận hành trước chu kỳ ngân sách mới.
